questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Provides less than half of a motorcycle's braking power.
Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's braking power.
Should not be used unless the road is wet.
Should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides about 70 percent of a motorcycle's braking power.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which colors help riders be seen the most?

options.text: Orange and red.
Green and blue.
Purple and gold.
Black and white.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange and red.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What should you NOT do to stay safe when riding at night?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Reduce your speed.
Use your high beam headlight when possible.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down, use your high beam headlight when not near other vehicles, and stay far behind the vehicle in front of you. Watch other vehicles' lights to learn about the road ahead.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Hold the handlebars loosely.
Gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
Increase your speed to leave the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and keep your motorcycle going straight as you slow down. If you need to brake, gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch located?

options.text: Near the left handlebar
Near the right handlebar
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handlebar
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is located next to the right handlebar. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: For eye or face shield protection to work well, it must have all of these qualities EXCEPT:

options.text: Fasten securely.
Be too tight to allow sunglasses or eyeglasses.
Be free of scratches.
Allow clear views to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be too tight to allow sunglasses or eyeglasses.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must have no scratches, be hard to break through, let you see clearly on both sides, fasten securely, let air flow to prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if you need them.

questions.question: The best sitting position when riding:

options.text: Requires your arms to hold you up.
Lets you reach the controls easily.
Keeps your arms straight when holding the handlebars.
Keeps your knees away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you reach the controls easily.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should bend slightly at the handlebars—do not stretch to reach them. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.

questions.question: Braking in a turn is:

options.text: Easier than braking on a straight road.
Harder than braking on a straight road.
Safe when using the front brake only.
Safe when using the rear brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes in a turn, but only if you know the correct technique and are very careful.

questions.question: If you can't avoid a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you can't avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and move across it as slowly as possible.

questions.question: You operate the gearshift lever with:

options.text: Your right hand.
Your right foot.
Your left hand.
Your left foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your left foot.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, what should you do?

options.text: Ride where the driver can see you in their mirror.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Do not worry about where you position yourself.
Always ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride where the driver can see you in their mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when behind a car. This position is most visible in the car's rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull over and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Do not ride down the center of the lane in wet conditions. Instead, ride in the tire tracks made by cars ahead of you. The left tire track often works best, but it depends on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, you should do everything except:

options.text: Clean the mirrors.
Test the horn.
Close the fuel supply valve.
Check that the clutch works smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the fuel supply valve.
questions.explanation: After mounting your motorcycle, check the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Keep the fuel supply valve open.

questions.question: How can you stop other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Weave back and forth in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage cars from trying to share it with you.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding.
When you will slow down where drivers won't expect it.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your turn signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down where drivers won't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are hard to see. Flash your brake light before slowing down in unexpected places, such as in the middle of a block or near an alley. This helps other drivers notice you are slowing.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up if you can.
Stay seated and lift your feet off the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle straight. Just before hitting it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: How do you get the shortest straight-line stop?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes and lock the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: On a straight road, use both brakes for the shortest stop. Avoid locking either brake.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is one benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance?

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance will not take much time.
Maintenance will be inexpensive.
Maintenance checks can prevent parking tickets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A well-maintained motorcycle will continue to ride like new. Regular maintenance should be part of your motorcycle's care routine.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, what should they do?

options.text: Lean when you lean.
Hold onto the seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when you lean.
questions.explanation: Passengers should lean when the driver leans. They should sit forward without crowding the driver and hold firmly onto the driver's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Before riding, you should check all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Fluids
Headlight and taillight
Turn signals
Reflectors

questions.correctAnswerText: Reflectors
questions.explanation: Before riding, do a thorough check of your motorcycle. Check the tires, oil, fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield
Only protects your eyes
Protects your whole face
Does not protect your face as well as goggles

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your whole face
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes, not the rest of your face. A windshield cannot replace a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Lean with the operator
Never touch the operator
Sit as far back on the seat as possible
Hold onto the seat

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the operator
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you during turns and curves. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: Intersections
Highways
Parking lots
Residential areas

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: The greatest risk of conflict between your motorcycle and other vehicles is at intersections. Be alert when another vehicle may cross in front of you.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: On short trips
On long trips
After at least one hour of riding
After more than 8 hours of riding

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts out.
